evidence.field: Glyph origin; phonetic-series table; Middle Chinese and Old Chinese reconstruction
evidence.text: The entry analyses 媽 as semantic 女 plus phonetic 馬, and reports Zhengzhang Shangfang (2003) Old Chinese 媽 *maːʔ and 馬 *mraːʔ. It gives Middle Chinese muX, fanqie 莫補切, and lists a ‘mare; female horse’ sense as obsolete and hapax. These are source-reported analyses and lexicographic claims, not proof that all senses share a single origin.

evidence.text: The entry explicitly identifies 妈 as simplified from 媽, with 馬 simplified to 马. This supports a simplified_form relation for the whole traditional graph and its phonetic component; it does not establish an earlier historical ancestor relation.
evidence.title: 妈 — Wiktionary

evidence.field: Chinese pronunciation; Middle Chinese and Old Chinese reconstruction
evidence.text: Reports Standard Mandarin mā; Middle Chinese muX (Baxter notation; rising tone X), with fanqie 莫補切; Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese /maːʔ/ for 媽 and /mraːʔ/ for 馬. In this reconstruction the initial nasal and broad rhyme resemblance make 馬 a plausible phonetic component despite the vowel difference. This is phonological comparison, not evidence from modern Mandarin alone.

gaps: The local repository rows requested for Unihan and Baxter–Sagart could not be checked in this browser-only research stage. In particular, the cited Wiktionary entry gives Baxter Middle Chinese muX, while dossier metadata gives Guangyun 明一模上 / fanqie 莫補; these are compatible descriptive records but not independently cross-checked against the local Baxter–Sagart file.

Official Unicode GetUnihanData pages for U+5ABD and U+5988 were attempted and inaccessible. Therefore exact current kMandarin rows were not verified or cited as successful evidence. A Unicode search interface was inspected only for what its kMandarin field means.

No inspected primary paleographic witness demonstrates an early form of 媽. The MOE reference explicitly says it is not in Shuowen; its shape table lists several paleographic resources as unavailable. No claim about oracle-bone, bronze, seal, clerical, or corruption stages is established here.

The MOE dictionary cites the 龍龕手鑑 gloss but the character-level image was not inspected. The dictionary is a Liao-period work dated 997 in secondary metadata found during search, but no primary page was opened to verify the date or exact witness. Thus the earliest dated attestation of the mother sense remains not independently verified from the primary source.

The entry's colloquial relation of 媽 to 母 and any proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan source are secondary etymological claims. This research did not independently establish the spoken-word genealogy or the semantic path from an older female/woman term to ‘mother’; graphic history and word history remain distinct.

Wiktionary lists an obsolete ‘mare’ sense without an inspected dated citation. Its date, relation to the mother sense, and whether this is an unrelated use remain unresolved; do not infer chronology from the list of glosses.

The phonetic analysis has system-specific support in Zhengzhang reconstructions, but no independent reconstruction-system comparison or local Baxter–Sagart row comparison was completed. Current Mandarin mā alone cannot establish the ancient sound relation.

No usable direct image URL with verified image identity and reuse rights was established. MOE's candidate image link failed; Commons and Xiaoxuetang searches did not produce a verified suitable image. Therefore no glyph candidates are proposed.

No primary paleographic witness for 媽 was visually inspected. The MOE entry states the character is absent from Shuowen and lists major oracle-bone, bronze, seal and other shape references as unavailable. No ancient formation stage or graphic corruption is established.

The 龍龕手鑑 mother gloss is cited by the MOE dictionary, but the target primary page image was not inspected. The opened volume page establishes attribution to Liao monk 行均 but does not display the 女部 passage. Earliest dated attestation is therefore not independently verified at primary-page level.

The proposed 女 semantic plus 馬 phonetic account is supported by dossier secondary excerpts and standard component analysis; no new source page with an independently inspectable sound-series argument was verified here. The source word for the 馬 graph is the word ‘horse’, but a sound-component claim does not depend on reconstructing an original depicted horse name. Local Baxter–Sagart data gives 馬 *mˤraʔ but contains no 媽 row, preventing same-system comparison.

The local Unihan rows establish current mā for 媽/妈 and mǎ for 馬. Character-specific Unicode records were inaccessible, so the required official click-through references could not be verified. The external Unihan search interface documents the property only generally.

Later uses for female elders, servants and older women are listed by the MOE dictionary, but their dates and semantic links to the mother address sense remain undated here. The reported ‘mare’ gloss in dossier Wiktionary evidence has no verified dated citation; its relationship to the mother sense remains unresolved.

The local source Baxter–Sagart row uses *mˤraʔ for 馬; dossier Wiktionary provides Zhengzhang's *mraːʔ for 馬 and *maːʔ for 媽. These are different reconstruction systems and must not be merged. Exact Zhengzhang host/component phonetic comparison was not independently rechecked during this run.
